status: Experimental durable coordinator-journal prefix decisions; not a replacement serving engine
behavior: Claims inherit the catalog from the exact compared predecessor
Discovery begins only after confirmed activation and drain; scans are opaque and bound to their root and catalog
A renewal can refresh the comparison during a scan only if the confirmed catalog is unchanged
All immutable uploads finish before the captured conditional publication; failed uploads send no register mutation
Lost publication replies recover the canonical decision through exact validation or a successful claim
Previously selected prefixes never extend to include late journal uploads
Missing or corrupt referenced objects fail recovery without becoming unselected history

storage.index: Existing immutable B+tree, 64 entries per page, maximum height 12; no small per-bucket entry cap
storage.memory_scope: Bounded object reads and one live frame per journal reader; callers must admit retained cursors and frames
storage.recovery_work: Traverses registration ancestry with indexed prefix lookup; no checkpoint truncation or bounded total recovery time

negative_controls: Publication before known durable upload violates DurableCatalog
coverage_controls: Third epoch inherits a prior selection

faults: Lost selection reply followed by late second frame, exact revalidation and complete controller replacement
Abandoned selection and successor claim in both provider-application orders
Stale parallel scans cannot replace a chosen prefix
Discovery before activation, incomplete scans, foreign owner and expired permission
Missing/corrupt header, page and prefix; checksum-valid invalid header fields; oversized header; cursor preservation
Lost or delayed upload at each of prefix, index and header stages sends no publication; late orphan arrival
130 decisions survive B+tree splitting and streaming recovery
Repeated renewals during a long scan preserve progress while catalog is unchanged
tests.b2_http: Applied selection response lost; one control attempt; exact validation recovers empty selected journal; file bytes use in-memory fixture
tests.s3_http: Real binding uploads/reads journal, registration, index, prefix and header; lost applied selection response; later frame excluded from selected replay

development_iteration.change: Only the disposable test-client server uses explicit bounded request budgets of 1000000 units/second and burst units
development_iteration.skip_reason: Opt-in all-process-kill Harness case requires a control fixture; separate qualification runner
development_iteration.scope: Single local measurements of avoided admission waits; not transaction throughput or a performance SLO

assumptions: Ordered winning epochs and discoverable immutable journal registrations
Drain completion ends all earlier acknowledgement permission; physical timing is abstracted
Atomic exact register comparison, durable immutable bytes and accurate positive object reads
Trusted storage/control credentials; no external deletion of live history
Fresh identities and the separately documented root timing and invocation contract
limitations: No theorem composes acquisition, registration, requests, physical clocks, catalog and data into the Rust implementation
No transaction/receipt/value-view recovery or replacement HTTP serving API
No system clock adapter, production timing profile, automatic renewal/election driver, placement or routing
No catalog/registration collection, checkpoint truncation or physical upload admission
Local and loopback fixtures; no new cloud benchmark or production-readiness claim
Current HTTP engine retains conditional read barriers
